summary: Internal engineering and product sync to validate Q4 launch readiness for model pinning + intelligent batching improvements. Discussed perf targets, canary rollout, QA regression, runbooks, and outstanding infra/security items. Agreed on owners and dates for final checks.
transcript: 00:00 Ava: Alright team, thanks everyone for joining, we'll kick off agenda is launch readiness for the Q4 release, model pinning and batching optimizations, uh, 55 minutes, let's run through checklist.
00:12 Dev: Quick note, have execs been looped in? Eli and Harper are on so we can ask clarifying Qs as we go.
00:20 Eli: yeah thanks, just here to hear risks and blockers, nothing to add unless there's a major hitch.
00:28 Ava: Great. First item, perf baseline. Sofia can you summarize where we are?

00:34 Sofia: Sure, so locally we've got the quantized path running, batching changes reduce per-token latency in batch sizes > 8, but single-shot P95 still about 180ms on p4d in our tests uh that was with the new kv cache change, sometimes transcribed as keyV cache in the logs, so ignore that typo and memory looks stable but we saw occasional GC spikes when serving long context.
01:05 Noah: Those GC spikes correlated with the e2e tests that had long system prompts, we have two flaky tests failing intermittently in staging.

01:12 Liam: On infra, I've increased the autoscaler threshold and added a temporary buffer for the canary fleet, but we need a rollback plan if model fallback trips during high traffic, currently can fallback to the r12-compat model which is slightly cheaper but also slower.
01:32 Dev: What's our perf target again? We said P95 under 200ms for hosted API on the dedicated pool right?
01:38 Sofia: Correct, target P95 <= 200ms for the common 0-512 token SKU. We hit 180ms in good runs but high variance at scale, need more load testing.
01:48 Ava: Load testing who owns it and when?
01:51 Sofia: I'll own it I'll run a 12-hour soak and a few spike tests and upload results to the benchmarks spreadsheet, aim to finish by next Wed, 11/11.
02:03 Maya: I'll make sure stakeholders have access to that sheet and the link in the launch email, so transparency for SRE and product ops.
02:10 Eli: Also call out cost impact in the sheet finance wants approx delta per 1M requests if we keep the current batch size and KV caching strategy.
02:20 Priya: yes I need that number to finalize the budget memo, if you can give a conservative estimate that'd be great.
02:27 Sofia: I'll add a cost column, rough ballpark now is +12-18% unit cost for the lower latency config, but caching reduces token compute for repeated prefixes so could be neutral long term.
02:40 Dev: Next, canary rollout plan. Liam?

02:43 Liam: Proposed: start with 2% traffic in region-us-west, monitor latency, error rate, and token cost. If stable for 24h, step to 10%, then 25% after 48h. Auto-fallback policy to previous model if error rate spikes > 1% or P95 increases >25%.
03:00 Ava: That sounds good. Add synthetic checks for KV cache miss rates and memory growth too.

03:08 Liam: Will add those. Also need to update oncall runbook with exact rollback commands and the feature-flag toggle path, I found a small mismatch in the playbook last time where we referenced the old API path.

03:20 Noah: QA: regression suite currently at 82% pass in staging. Two flaky tests (concurrency) and one determinism check failing intermittently. I can prioritize flake fixes but need engineering help to root cause.
03:34 Sofia: I'll pair on the concurrency flake tomorrow, likely a race in KV cache warmup path might be timing dependent on the batching warmup.
03:41 Noah: cool if we fix them we can schedule a full regression run, then smoke tests on the canary infra.
03:48 Ava: Security/compliance, any open items?

03:51 Dev: SOC2 doc updates were pushed last week; we still need the KMS key rotation notes for Private customers doc, and a quick readout for the security review signoff. Harper, do you want a separate session?

04:03 Harper: Security team is fine with scheduled signoff but want the encryption at rest matrix, also confirm whether we ship any telemetry that includes prompt text we should ensure redact-by-default for PII.
04:16 Sofia: We do not persist raw prompts in logs, only anonymized hashes for debugging, but I'll add the explicit line to the compliance doc.
04:24 Ava: Good. Docs and customer comms Maya, can you draft the pre-launch note and the known-limits section?
04:30 Maya: On it, will include expected latency ranges, known flakiness with extremely long contexts, and recommended batch tuning knobs.
04:38 Dev: One more product ask we had request to support per-route model pinning; is that in scope?
04:44 Sofia: The runtime change is minimal, config layer needs an API flag. We can ship a beta with caveats, but it does increase config surface and rollout complexity.
04:54 Ava: Decision needed: ship beta now or delay to patch in 2 weeks?
04:58 Eli: If beta doesn't impact latency or risk rollback complexity, we can ship, but prefer a canary with opt-in routes only. Finance prefers less delay.
05:10 Dev: Let's do opt-in beta behind a feature flag; add to the canary checklist to only enable for internal test routes first.
05:16 Sofia: Agreed.
05:18 Ava: Okay checklist recap Sofia perf baseline, Noah regression, Liam runbooks and canary config, Maya comms, Ava finalize checklist. Anything else?
05:27 Priya: Budget note pending the cost delta, will review once Sofia adds the cost column.
05:33 Liam: I'll also schedule a 30min oncall dry-run next Monday to exercise rollback commands.
05:39 Noah: And I'll run the smoke test after the first 2% canary bump, will report to #release-status.
05:45 Ava: Great. Any blockers that should stop the launch?
05:49 Sofia: Major blocker would be persistent memory growth in long-context workloads if that shows up in soak tests, we pause.
05:56 Dev: Also unresolved security audit items could pause, but looks manageable.
06:02 Ava: Alright let's reconvene next Monday for pre-launch check. I'll send calendar invite for 30 minutes. Thanks everyone.
06:10 Eli: Thanks, appreciate the clarity.
06:14 Harper: Thanks all.
06:18 End of transcript
